title: Bridging Textual-Collaborative Gap through Semantic Codes for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Sequential recommender systems need to leverage item textual metadata together with ID-based collaborative information.

gap.claim: Existing methods that combine text and ID representations struggle to balance textual information with collaborative information from sequential user behavior.

contributions.claim: CCFRec is a code-based textual and collaborative semantic fusion method for sequential recommendation.

The method generates fine-grained semantic codes from multi-view text embeddings using vector quantization and uses a cross-attention code-guided module to extract and integrate relevant textual information.
The method introduces code masking objectives for masked code modeling and masked sequence alignment to enhance fusion of textual and collaborative semantics.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present CCFRec as a novel code-based textual and collaborative semantic fusion method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four public datasets reportedly demonstrate that CCFRec significantly improves over various sequential recommendation models.
The authors report that their code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation research combines item side information with ID-based collaborative information, with this study focusing on textual metadata.
Existing text-and-ID methods have difficulty balancing textual and sequential collaborative information.
CCFRec bridges the two information sources with semantic codes, vector-quantized multi-view text embeddings, and cross-attention fusion.
Code masking with masked code modeling and masked sequence alignment is used to improve semantic fusion and sequence modeling.
The authors report significant improvements on four public datasets and provide code availability.

source_observation.claim: Semantic codes are used to bridge textual and collaborative information in sequential recommendation.

interpretation.claim: An intermediate semantic representation may help coordinate heterogeneous item and behavior signals.

application.claim: Consider discrete or quantized semantic representations when integrating metadata with sequential behavioral signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when semantic codes outperform alternative fusion strategies or how they behave across domains.

source_observation.claim: Masked code modeling and masked sequence alignment are used to capture within-item code correlations and improve sequence modeling.

interpretation.claim: Auxiliary masking objectives may encourage alignment between item-level semantics and sequence-level collaborative patterns.

application.claim: Use complementary masking objectives when training a model to fuse item semantics with behavioral sequences.

exception.claim: The abstract does not report the individual contribution of either objective or the conditions under which masking is beneficial.

unknowns: The four public datasets are not identified.
Evaluation metrics, baseline identities, numerical results, and statistical significance details are not provided.
Ablation results and implementation details are not provided.
